articleHeadline: Flesh-eating bacteria attack a man's brain
articleSummary: Whitmore disease (melioidosis) caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei infected a 54-year-old man in Ninh Bình, Vietnam. articleHeadline: Model Suggests Strategy Cuts Simulated Mpox by 97.8%
articleSummary: Mpox (Monkeypox) transmission modeled in Indonesia by Hasanuddin University researchers to explore multi-measure outbreak control. The two-population model tracks humans (nine infection-stage groups) and rodents (three groups), including asymptomatic human infections and latent rodent infections. Four interventions—vaccination (reduces susceptibility), treatment (promotes recovery/reduces impact), quarantine (reduces contacts), and educational campaigns (promotes protective behavior)—are tested alone and in combination. The full four–intervention strategy achieves a 97.85% reduction in total human infections versus no intervention and is the most cost-effective scenario. Early-phase emphasis on quarantine and education, with vaccination and treatment maintained from outbreak start, yields best results across stages. The model identifies Mpox-free and endemic equilibria; rodent transmission can sustain long-term persistence, signaling rodents as a reservoir and highlighting a One Health approach.
